sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Gradient Boosting (python-gradient-boosting) is a credit default classifier that predicts default.payment.next.month on the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset. Its business purpose is recorded as a challenger compared against the production default model that informs but does not drive decisions, but this purpose and the input feature list are marked as inferred rather than confirmed. The business owner, intended use, decision context, decision threshold and whether the model is used in production or only for comparison are not documented.

rows.label: Dataset
rows.value: Default of Credit Card Clients (UCI Machine Learning Repository)

rows.label: Origin
rows.value: Credit-card clients in Taiwan, payment history April to September 2005

rows.label: Intended use here
rows.value: Public demonstration data only; not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn GradientBoostingClassifier with default hyperparameters and random_state set to a seed that defaults to 42. It is trained on a stratified 80/20 train/test split (random_state=42) of the 30,000-record dataset, after validation checks on row count, column count, missing values and default rate. It uses 21 predictors (credit limit, education, marriage, repayment status, bill amounts and payment amounts), excluding ID, SEX and AGE, with no scaling or encoding applied. No class imbalance handling or hyperparameter tuning is performed, and the rationale for using defaults is not documented.

rows.label: Preprocessing
rows.value: Fetch UCI dataset 350 via ucimlrepo and rename generic X1..X23 columns to the expected feature names, Validate dataset: 30,000 rows, 25 columns, no missing values, default rate between 0.20 and 0.24, Separate target default.payment.next.month and cast it to int, Stratified train/test split, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, Drop ID, SEX and AGE from the predictors (predictive_features), No scaling or encoding applied to this model (StandardScaler is used only in the logistic regression pipeline)

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: No performance, fairness, stability or monitoring results exist for this model; those reports cover only the statsmodels candidate, and no decision threshold is set. SHAP explanations are computed on only the first 500 test rows. The training data is public demonstration data on credit-card clients in Taiwan (April to September 2005) and is not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio. Software and library versions and a model-specific monitoring plan are not documented, and SEX and AGE are assumed to be fairness-only attributes.
